option_description: Whether the IdP's token/assertion signing private keys are protected by an HSM or KMS as non-exportable material rather than stored as plaintext key files on disk.
security_impact: Triggers "Signing-key compromise / golden token / golden SAML" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when keys_managed_in_hsm_or_kms is false. A disk-resident static signing key an attacker can steal yields golden-token / golden-SAML forgery for any user across every federated RP (T1606.002 / T1649).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the realm signing-key providers and confirm the active key material is HSM/KMS-backed (non-exportable) rather than a plaintext rsa-generated key on disk.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Realm Settings > Keys > Providers
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An rsa/rsa-generated provider with rotation; old keys shown as passive, not a single permanent active key
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide (regularly rotate keys); OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review where the active signing private key actually lives — confirm it is held in an HSM/KMS as non-exportable material (NIST SP 800-63C requires FIPS 140 L1+ signing keys at AAL3/government AAL2), not a key file on the filesystem.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key custody documented as HSM/KMS-resident and non-exportable; no plaintext private-key file readable on the IdP host

option_description: Whether the realm signing keys (JWKS) are rotated on a schedule with superseded keys retired to passive, bounding the forgery window of a leaked key.
security_impact: Triggers "Signing-key compromise / golden token / golden SAML" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when key_rotation_enabled is false. A single static key never rotated gives a stolen signing key indefinite golden-token capability (T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the realm Keys providers for scheduled rotation with superseded keys retired to passive.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Realm Settings > Keys > Providers
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An rsa/rsa-generated provider with rotation; old keys shown as passive, not a single permanent active key
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide (regularly rotate keys); OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether the token/assertion signing key is generated with adequate cryptographic strength and entropy (adequate asymmetric key size from a strong RNG, FIPS 140 backed per NIST SP 800-63C).
security_impact: Triggers "Signing-key compromise / golden token / golden SAML" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when signing_key_high_entropy is false. A weak/low-entropy signing key can be recovered or brute-forced, enabling token/assertion forgery (T1606).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the active signing-key provider's key size/type in the realm Keys providers; confirm an adequately-sized asymmetric key (e.g. RSA >= 2048 / EC P-256+).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Realm Settings > Keys > Providers (key size / type column)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Asymmetric key of adequate size (RSA >= 2048 or EC P-256+); not an undersized or symmetric key
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide (regularly rotate keys); OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the signing key was generated from a strong RNG and is FIPS 140 backed where required by the AAL (NIST SP 800-63C).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key generation documented as strong-RNG / FIPS 140 backed at the required AAL

option_description: Whether the IdP/verifier pins an expected asymmetric signing algorithm (RS256/ES256/PS256) server-side per RFC 8725 instead of trusting the token's own 'alg' header, and never advertises or accepts 'alg:none' or symmetric HS256.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of TWO exposures (fires when signature_algorithm_pinned_server_side is false): "Signing-key compromise / golden token / golden SAML" and "JWT algorithm confusion / alg:none / RS256->HS256". Header-driven algorithm selection enables RS256->HS256 key-confusion and alg:none forgery (T1606 / T1134.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the per-client Access/ID Token Signature Algorithm and confirm an asymmetric algorithm is fixed (the verifier does not select from the token's own alg header).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Advanced > Fine Grain OpenID Connect Configuration > Access Token / ID Token Signature Algorithm
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RS256 or ES256; HS256/none is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 8725 JWT BCP

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the OIDC discovery document for the advertised signing algorithms; presence of HS256/none indicates the verifier may not pin an asymmetric algorithm.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Includes RS256/ES256; presence of HS256/none as an advertised/acceptable value is a concern

option_description: Whether inbound federation trusts (identity-provider / SAML SP relationships and their signing certificates) are explicitly validated and pinned, so a rogue trust cannot inject attacker-controlled signing material.
security_impact: Triggers "Signing-key compromise / golden token / golden SAML" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when federation_trust_validated is false. The rogue-trust path of golden SAML (SolarWinds/UNC2452) lets an attacker forge assertions for any user (T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review each configured Identity Provider brokering entry and its signing certificate; confirm trusts are explicitly pinned and metadata is not auto-accepted from attacker-supplied sources.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Identity Providers > {provider} (signing certificate / validate signature settings)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each inbound trust has a pinned/validated signing certificate; no auto-accept of unverified federation metadata

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the IdP owners on how new inbound federation trusts are onboarded — confirm signing material is verified out-of-band and pinned (NIST SP 800-63C federation trust establishment).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented trust-establishment procedure with out-of-band certificate verification; no self-service rogue-trust path

option_description: Whether the IdP enforces exact-string matching of each client's Valid Redirect URIs (no wildcard '*', no overly-broad host/path, no http://localhost or 127.0.0.1 entries in production) per RFC 9700.
security_impact: Triggers "Lax redirect_uri / open-redirect code theft" — its sole OR-condition — firing when redirect_uri_exact_match_enforced is false. Wildcard/loopback/path-traversable redirect URIs let an attacker exfiltrate the authorization code/token (account takeover; Keycloak CVE-2024-8883 / CVE-2024-1132 / CVE-2023-6927; T1190 / T1550.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect each client's Valid Redirect URIs and confirm every entry is a single exact absolute https URI.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Settings > Valid Redirect URIs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each entry is a single exact URI; no '*' segments and no localhost/127.0.0.1 entries
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide (Mitigating Security Threats — unspecific redirect URIs)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the per-client redirectUris allow-list via the admin REST API and check no element is a wildcard or loopback host in production.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No element contains '*' or a localhost host in production
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 9700 OAuth 2.0 Security BCP (exact redirect_uri matching)

option_description: Whether the IdP issues or accepts JWTs whose JOSE 'alg' header is 'none' (unsigned tokens). RFC 8725 requires rejecting 'none'.
security_impact: Triggers "JWT algorithm confusion / alg:none / RS256->HS256" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when accepts_alg_none is true. Honouring unsigned tokens lets an attacker strip the signature and forge arbitrary tokens (T1606 / T1134.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the OIDC discovery document — an advertised/acceptable 'none' value signals the verifier may honour unsigned tokens.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Includes RS256/ES256; presence of HS256/none as an advertised/acceptable value is a concern

how_to_obtain.instruction: Craft a test token with the JOSE header set to {"alg":"none"} (signature stripped) and present it to a protected endpoint; confirm the verifier rejects it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The endpoint rejects the alg:none token (401/invalid_token); acceptance is insecure

option_description: Whether the verifier selects the HMAC/RSA verification routine from the token's own 'alg' header rather than a pinned expected algorithm, permitting an RS256->HS256 switch signed with the IdP's public key.
security_impact: Triggers "JWT algorithm confusion / alg:none / RS256->HS256" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when rs256_to_hs256_confusion_possible is true. Header-driven routine selection lets an attacker forge tokens by signing HS256 with the known public key (T1606 / T1134.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the per-client signature algorithm is a fixed asymmetric value (RS*/ES*/PS*) so the verifier cannot be steered to HMAC by the token's alg header.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Advanced > Fine Grain OpenID Connect Configuration > Access Token / ID Token Signature Algorithm
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RS256 or ES256; HS256/none is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 8725 JWT BCP

how_to_obtain.instruction: Take an RS256 token, re-sign it as HS256 using the IdP's published JWKS public key as the HMAC secret, and present it; confirm the verifier rejects the algorithm switch.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The verifier rejects the HS256-resigned token; acceptance proves RS256->HS256 confusion is possible

option_description: Per-client access/ID token signature algorithm. Asymmetric RS*/ES*/PS* are secure (RPs verify via public JWKS); symmetric HS* enables RS256->HS256 key-confusion forgery and 'none' is never acceptable.
security_impact: Triggers "JWT algorithm confusion / alg:none / RS256->HS256" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when access_token_signature_algorithm is in [HS256, HS384, HS512, none]. A symmetric/none algorithm enables forgery against every RP that trusts the IdP (T1606 / T1134.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the per-client token signature algorithm under Fine Grain OpenID Connect Configuration.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Advanced > Fine Grain OpenID Connect Configuration > Access Token / ID Token Signature Algorithm
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RS256 or ES256; HS256/none is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 8725 JWT BCP

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the advertised signing algorithms from OIDC discovery as a realm-wide cross-check.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Includes RS256/ES256; presence of HS256/none as an advertised/acceptable value is a concern

option_description: Whether Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) is enforced for the OAuth/OIDC authorization-code flow on this client. RFC 9700 mandates PKCE for ALL client types.
security_impact: Triggers "Insecure OAuth flow / authorization-code interception without PKCE" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when pkce_required is false. Without PKCE an intercepted authorization code can be redeemed by an attacker (T1550.001 / T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the per-client PKCE Code Challenge Method is set (not blank), enforcing PKCE for the authorization-code flow.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Advanced > Advanced Settings > Proof Key for Code Exchange Code Challenge Method
how_to_obtain.expected_output: S256 (secure); blank means PKCE not enforced for this client
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 7636 PKCE

option_description: Whether PKCE is enforced specifically with the S256 (SHA-256) code-challenge method rather than the weak 'plain' method.
security_impact: Triggers "Insecure OAuth flow / authorization-code interception without PKCE" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when pkce_method_s256_required is false. The 'plain' method transmits the verifier-equivalent in the clear, removing the code-binding protection (T1550.001 / T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the per-client Code Challenge Method is fixed to S256 (not 'plain').
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Advanced > Advanced Settings > Proof Key for Code Exchange Code Challenge Method
how_to_obtain.expected_output: S256 (secure); blank means PKCE not enforced for this client
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 7636 PKCE

option_description: Whether the IdP accepts the deprecated 'plain' PKCE code-challenge method (alongside or instead of S256). 'plain' offers no protection against a passive observer of the challenge.
security_impact: Triggers "Insecure OAuth flow / authorization-code interception without PKCE" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when code_challenge_method_plain_accepted is true. Accepting 'plain' negates PKCE's defence against code interception (T1550.001 / T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the per-client Code Challenge Method is fixed to S256 so 'plain' is not an accepted method.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Advanced > Advanced Settings > Proof Key for Code Exchange Code Challenge Method
how_to_obtain.expected_output: S256 (secure); blank means PKCE not enforced for this client
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 7636 PKCE

how_to_obtain.instruction: Initiate an authorization-code request with code_challenge_method=plain and confirm the IdP refuses it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The IdP rejects the 'plain' challenge method (only S256 honoured); acceptance is insecure

option_description: Whether either the deprecated Implicit grant (token in URL fragment, no PKCE) or the Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC / Direct Access Grants) grant is enabled on this client. RFC 9700 deprecates both.
security_impact: Triggers "Insecure OAuth flow / authorization-code interception without PKCE" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when implicit_or_ropc_grant_enabled is true. Implicit exposes tokens in the URL with no code-exchange protection; ROPC makes the client handle the raw password and bypasses MFA/consent/federation (T1550.001 / T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the client's Capability config for the Implicit flow toggle.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Settings > Capability config > Implicit flow
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Implicit flow = Off; Standard flow = On
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 9700 (implicit grant deprecated)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the client's Capability config for the Direct Access Grants (ROPC) toggle.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Settings > Capability config > Direct access grants
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Direct access grants = Off
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 9700 (ROPC deprecated)

option_description: Whether the OAuth 'state' parameter is generated, bound to the user's session, and verified on the authorization-response callback (RFC 6749 CSRF defence on the redirect endpoint).
security_impact: Triggers "Insecure OAuth flow / authorization-code interception without PKCE" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when oauth_state_bound_and_verified is false. An unbound/unverified state enables login-CSRF on the redirect endpoint (T1550.001 / T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the authorization request/response for the client and confirm a unique 'state' is sent and that tampering with or omitting it on the callback is rejected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A unique state is present on the request and the callback rejects a mismatched/missing state

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the relying-party client integration code/library to confirm it generates, stores in session, and verifies the state parameter on callback (state binding is an RP responsibility).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RP code generates and verifies a session-bound state per RFC 6749

option_description: Whether the OIDC 'nonce' claim is sent on the authentication request and validated against the returned ID token, defeating ID-token replay (OIDC Core requirement).
security_impact: Triggers "Insecure OAuth flow / authorization-code interception without PKCE" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when oidc_nonce_validated is false. Without nonce validation an ID token can be replayed (T1550.001 / T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture an OIDC authentication request and the returned ID token; confirm a nonce is sent and matches the 'nonce' claim in the ID token the RP validates.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The request carries a nonce and the RP validates it against the ID token's nonce claim

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the RP integration to confirm nonce generation and validation against the returned ID token (an RP-side OIDC Core requirement).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RP code sends and validates the nonce per OIDC Core

option_description: Whether the IdP signs SAML assertions AND the relying party cryptographically verifies that signature over the full assertion with XML signature-wrapping defences.
security_impact: Triggers "SAML assertion forgery / signature-wrapping / replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when saml_assertion_signature_verified is false. Unsigned/unverified assertions can be forged or signature-wrapped to impersonate any user (golden SAML; T1606.002 / T1134.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the SAML client's signing capabilities — confirm Sign Assertions and Client signature required are On.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {saml-client} > Settings > SAML capabilities: Sign Assertions / Sign Documents / Client signature required / Encrypt Assertions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Sign Assertions On; signature required On; assertions encrypted where confidentiality required
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP SAML Security Cheat Sheet; NIST SP 800-63C-4 (FAL1 signed / FAL2 encrypted)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SP verifies the signature over the full assertion with signature-wrapping defences (canonical reference resolution, single-assertion enforcement).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP rejects assertions whose signature does not cover the full assertion / contains injected sibling assertions

option_description: Whether every issued assertion carries an AudienceRestriction naming the specific intended SP EntityID and the SP rejects assertions whose audience does not exactly match itself.
security_impact: Triggers "SAML assertion forgery / signature-wrapping / replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when saml_audience_restriction_strict is false. An assertion minted for one SP can be replayed at another to impersonate the user (NIST SP 800-63C; T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decode an issued SAML assertion and inspect the AudienceRestriction; confirm it names the specific SP EntityID (not missing/empty or shared/wildcard).
how_to_obtain.command: Decode an issued access/ID token (e.g. jwt decode) and inspect aud, iss, exp claims
how_to_obtain.expected_output: aud == the specific client_id/RP; iss == IdP issuer URL; exp present and short
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63C-4 (audience restriction, signed assertions); OpenID Connect Core ID Token validation

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SP rejects assertions whose Audience does not exactly match its own EntityID (per-RP audience binding enforced at the consumer).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP rejects an assertion whose AudienceRestriction names a different SP

option_description: Whether the SP binds each assertion to its originating request by validating SubjectConfirmationData Recipient == its ACS URL and InResponseTo == the in-flight AuthnRequest ID, rejecting unsolicited/mismatched responses.
security_impact: Triggers "SAML assertion forgery / signature-wrapping / replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when saml_recipient_inresponseto_matched is false. An attacker can inject an unsolicited or stolen assertion at the SP (forced-login / assertion-injection; T1606.002 / T1134.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the SP's SAML response handling and confirm it validates Recipient == its ACS URL and InResponseTo == the in-flight AuthnRequest ID, rejecting unsolicited responses.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP rejects responses with a mismatched Recipient/InResponseTo or with no matching outstanding AuthnRequest

how_to_obtain.instruction: Replay a captured assertion to the SP's ACS with no matching outstanding AuthnRequest and confirm it is refused.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP refuses the unsolicited/injected assertion

option_description: Whether the SP maintains a replay cache keyed on assertion ID (and enforces NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter Conditions) so a previously-consumed, still-valid assertion cannot be presented twice.
security_impact: Triggers "SAML assertion forgery / signature-wrapping / replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when saml_assertion_replay_cache_active is false. A captured valid assertion can be replayed to re-authenticate as the victim (NIST SP 800-63C; T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SP maintains an assertion-ID replay cache and enforces NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter Conditions (one-time use within the validity window).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP rejects a second presentation of the same assertion ID and assertions outside the Conditions window

how_to_obtain.instruction: Present the same still-valid assertion twice to the SP and confirm the second presentation is rejected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Second presentation of the assertion is refused (replay blocked)

option_description: Whether every assertion/token the IdP mints carries a per-RP audience (aud) bound to the specific requesting client/RP, and that audience is the binding all RPs check.
security_impact: Triggers "Missing audience restriction / cross-RP token replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when audience_claim_validated is false. A token minted for one RP can be replayed at another (NIST SP 800-63C; T1550.001 / T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decode an issued access/ID token and confirm the 'aud' claim is the specific requesting client_id (not missing/empty or shared/wildcard).
how_to_obtain.command: Decode an issued access/ID token (e.g. jwt decode) and inspect aud, iss, exp claims
how_to_obtain.expected_output: aud == the specific client_id/RP; iss == IdP issuer URL; exp present and short
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63C-4 (audience restriction, signed assertions); OpenID Connect Core ID Token validation

option_description: Whether issued assertions/tokens carry the IdP issuer (iss) claim and the signature covers iss, so a token cannot be passed off as originating from a different trusted issuer.
security_impact: Triggers "Missing audience restriction / cross-RP token replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when issuer_claim_validated is false. Absent/unsigned iss weakens the iss/aud/sub/exp signed binding NIST SP 800-63C requires (T1550.001 / T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decode an issued token and confirm an 'iss' claim is present and equals the IdP issuer URL (and is covered by the signature).
how_to_obtain.command: Decode an issued access/ID token (e.g. jwt decode) and inspect aud, iss, exp claims
how_to_obtain.expected_output: aud == the specific client_id/RP; iss == IdP issuer URL; exp present and short
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63C-4 (audience restriction, signed assertions); OpenID Connect Core ID Token validation

option_description: Whether issued assertions/tokens carry an expiration (exp) claim covered by the issuer signature, so a captured token cannot be replayed indefinitely.
security_impact: Triggers "Missing audience restriction / cross-RP token replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when expiry_claim_validated is false. Missing/unsigned exp removes the time bound on a replayable token (T1550.001 / T1606.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decode an issued token and confirm an 'exp' claim is present (short-lived) and covered by the signature.
how_to_obtain.command: Decode an issued access/ID token (e.g. jwt decode) and inspect aud, iss, exp claims
how_to_obtain.expected_output: aud == the specific client_id/RP; iss == IdP issuer URL; exp present and short
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63C-4 (audience restriction, signed assertions); OpenID Connect Core ID Token validation

option_description: Whether multi-factor authentication is configured/available and required in the IdP login browser flow rather than password-only.
security_impact: Triggers "Weak / phishable MFA and credential brute force on the IdP" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when mfa_available is false. Password-only login leaves the front door open to credential stuffing and brute force (T1110 / T1621 / T1598.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the browser authentication flow and Required Actions; confirm an MFA execution (OTP/WebAuthn) is required, not merely optional.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Authentication > Flows (browser flow) — WebAuthn/OTP required; Required Actions: Configure OTP / WebAuthn enabled
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An MFA execution is REQUIRED (not Alternative/Disabled) in the flow used by admins
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63B Rev 4 (AAL2/AAL3, phishing-resistant); CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA

option_description: Whether the IdP requires a phishing-resistant authenticator (FIDO2/WebAuthn or PKI) rather than accepting phishable factors (SMS OTP / push).
security_impact: Triggers "Weak / phishable MFA and credential brute force on the IdP" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when phishing_resistant_authenticator_required is false. Phishable-only MFA lets an AiTM proxy harvest password + OTP/push and mint an IdP session (T1598.003 / T1621).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the authentication flow and confirm a phishing-resistant authenticator (WebAuthn/FIDO2 or PKI) is required, not merely offered alongside phishable SMS OTP/push.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Authentication > Flows (browser flow) — WebAuthn/OTP required; Required Actions: Configure OTP / WebAuthn enabled
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An MFA execution is REQUIRED (not Alternative/Disabled) in the flow used by admins
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63B Rev 4 (AAL2/AAL3, phishing-resistant); CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA

option_description: Whether MFA is REQUIRED (not Alternative/Disabled) in the authentication flow used by realm/admin accounts.
security_impact: Triggers "Weak / phishable MFA and credential brute force on the IdP" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when admin_mfa_enforced is false. IdP admin compromise yields golden-token control of the whole federation, so admin MFA is the highest-value facet (T1110 / T1621).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm MFA is set to Required (not Alternative/Disabled) in the realm/admin authentication flow.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Authentication > Flows (browser flow) — WebAuthn/OTP required; Required Actions: Configure OTP / WebAuthn enabled
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An MFA execution is REQUIRED (not Alternative/Disabled) in the flow used by admins
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63B Rev 4 (AAL2/AAL3, phishing-resistant); CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA

option_description: Whether brute-force detection (temporary lockout / increasing backoff) or upstream rate limiting is enabled on the IdP login/token endpoints.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of TWO exposures (fires when rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled is false): "Weak / phishable MFA and credential brute force on the IdP" (T1110) and "IdP availability / DoS (single point of failure)" (T1498 / T1499.003). Without it, login attempts are unlimited (credential stuffing) and request volume is unbounded (application-layer DoS).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the realm Security Defenses for Brute Force Detection (it is disabled by default in Keycloak).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Realm Settings > Security Defenses > Brute Force Detection
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enabled with a failure threshold and lockout/wait policy
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide (Mitigating Security Threats)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm any upstream gateway/WAF rate limiting fronting the public auth/token endpoints bounds request volume in addition to Keycloak's lockout.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Gateway/WAF rate limiting documented on /realms/*/protocol/* auth and token endpoints

option_description: Whether the IdP password policy screens proposed/credential passwords against known-breached corpora so credential reuse is blocked at the source.
security_impact: Triggers "Weak / phishable MFA and credential brute force on the IdP" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when breached_password_screening_enabled is false. Permitting known-breached passwords raises credential-stuffing success against the IdP (T1110 / NIST SP 800-63B blocklist).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the realm password policy for a breached/compromised-password (blocklist) check.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Authentication > Policies > Password policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A breached/compromised-password (or 'not recently used' / blocklist) policy entry is present per NIST SP 800-63B

option_description: Whether the IdP rotates the refresh token on each use with reuse-detection (Keycloak 'Revoke Refresh Token' On with a small Refresh Token Reuse Count).
security_impact: Triggers "Refresh-token theft without rotation" — appearing in two of its OR-groups (firing when refresh_token_rotation_enabled is false, including the AND-group with sender_constrained false). Without rotation a replayed stolen token is never flagged as compromise (RFC 9700; T1550.001 / T1528).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm 'Revoke Refresh Token' is enabled at the realm Tokens settings with a small allowed reuse count (rotation + reuse detection).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Realm Settings > Tokens > Revoke Refresh Token
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enabled, with a small allowed Refresh Token Reuse Count
how_to_obtain.source: Keycloak Server Administration Guide; RFC 9700 (refresh-token rotation with reuse detection)

option_description: Whether the IdP can revoke an issued refresh token server-side (token revocation / session-bound invalidation) so a detected-compromised or reused token is actively killed.
security_impact: Triggers "Refresh-token theft without rotation" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when server_side_revocation_supported is false. Without it even a flagged refresh token remains valid until natural expiry, sustaining indefinite stolen-token access (T1550.001 / T1528).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the IdP advertises a token revocation endpoint in OIDC discovery and that revoking a refresh token there immediately invalidates it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A revocation_endpoint URL is present and revoking a refresh token there kills subsequent use

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm server-side session invalidation is available (admin can log out a user's sessions, killing associated refresh tokens).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Users > {user} > Sessions (Logout) / Realm Settings > Sessions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admin logout invalidates the user's sessions and bound refresh tokens

option_description: Whether issued tokens are sender-constrained (DPoP per RFC 9449 or mTLS per RFC 8705) so a bearer token exfiltrated from a legitimate client cannot be presented from an attacker's machine.
security_impact: Triggers "Refresh-token theft without rotation" — it is one half of that exposure's AND-group (firing when sender_constrained is false AND refresh_token_rotation_enabled is false). A non-sender-constrained token is a pure bearer credential usable anywhere (RFC 9449/8705; T1550.001 / T1528).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check OIDC discovery for DPoP support (dpop_signing_alg_values_supported) and inspect whether issued tokens carry a cnf (confirmation) claim binding them to a key.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DPoP algorithms advertised and/or mTLS-bound tokens enabled; issued tokens carry a cnf claim

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm clients are configured for DPoP or mTLS sender-constraining (note: this is an advanced facet not exposed as a single Keycloak realm toggle).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Clients documented as DPoP- or mTLS-bound (RFC 9449 / RFC 8705)

option_description: Whether at least one OAuth/OIDC client has 'Full Scope Allowed' enabled, so its tokens carry every realm role regardless of need.
security_impact: Triggers "Over-broad client scopes / over-privileged clients" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when full_scope_allowed_clients is true. A single such client's compromise yields broad federated access, violating least privilege (T1078 / T1550.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect each client's Scope tab for the 'Full Scope Allowed' toggle; flag any client where it is On.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Client scopes / Scope tab > Full Scope Allowed
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Off, with only the needed client scopes assigned

option_description: Whether per-client scopes/roles are explicitly mapped to only what each client needs, rather than every client receiving the full set of realm roles.
security_impact: Triggers "Over-broad client scopes / over-privileged clients" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when scopes_least_privilege is false. Over-privileged clients carry tokens far beyond need so one client's compromise yields broad access (T1078 / T1550.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect each client's assigned client scopes and confirm only the needed scopes/roles are mapped (no blanket realm-role grants).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Clients > {client} > Client scopes / Scope tab > Full Scope Allowed
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Off, with only the needed client scopes assigned

option_description: Keycloak per-realm 'Require SSL' (sslRequired) controlling whether the IdP refuses non-TLS requests to its login, token, and admin endpoints. 'none' (the Keycloak default) accepts plaintext.
security_impact: Triggers "Unencrypted IdP transport" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when ssl_required equals 'none'. Plaintext exposes credentials, authorization codes, and tokens to sniffing/MITM on an adjacent network path (T1040 / T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the realm 'Require SSL' setting.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Realm Settings > General > Require SSL
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'All requests' (secure) or 'External requests' (acceptable); 'None' is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read sslRequired from the realm via the admin REST API.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: "sslRequired":"all" or "external"; "none" is insecure

option_description: Whether the IdP serves its login/token/admin endpoints exclusively over TLS and refuses any plaintext HTTP connection.
security_impact: Triggers "Unencrypted IdP transport" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when tls_only_transport is false. Cleartext acceptance anywhere on the path exposes credentials/codes/tokens to sniffing and AiTM (T1040 / T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the IdP endpoints over plaintext HTTP and confirm they refuse or redirect to HTTPS rather than serving content over cleartext.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connection refused or a 301/308 redirect to https://; a 200 over plaintext is insecure

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the realm 'Require SSL' setting which governs whether plaintext is accepted.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Admin Console > Realm Settings > General > Require SSL
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'All requests' (secure) or 'External requests' (acceptable); 'None' is insecure

option_description: Whether the IdP's TLS listener still negotiates deprecated protocol versions (TLS 1.0 / TLS 1.1 / SSLv3) below the TLS 1.2+ secure floor.
security_impact: Triggers "Unencrypted IdP transport" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when weak_tls_versions_enabled is true. Deprecated versions are vulnerable to downgrade and known cipher attacks, weakening the transport even when TLS is nominally enabled (T1040 / T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the negotiable TLS protocol versions on the IdP listener and confirm TLS 1.0/1.1/SSLv3 are not offered.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLSv1.2 / TLSv1.3 negotiable; no TLSv1.0/1.1 or SSLv3

option_description: Whether the IdP emits an HTTP Strict-Transport-Security response header so browsers are pinned to HTTPS and an SSL-strip / first-request downgrade on the login flow is prevented.
security_impact: Triggers "Unencrypted IdP transport" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when hsts_enforced is false. Without HSTS the initial navigation is downgradeable to cleartext (T1040 / T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Fetch the IdP login page headers over HTTPS and confirm a Strict-Transport-Security header is present.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A Strict-Transport-Security header (with a non-trivial max-age) is returned; absence is insecure

option_description: Whether the IdP software is running at or above the fixed release for all applicable published advisories (e.g. Keycloak >= 25.0.6 / 24.0.8 / 22.0.13 for CVE-2024-8883).
security_impact: Triggers "IdP software exploitation (unpatched CVE)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when software_version_patched is false. An unpatched internet-facing IdP is a prime exploitation target for redirect bypass / auth bypass / RCE (T1190 / T1212).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read systemInfo.version from server info and compare against the vendor advisory fixed-version list.
how_to_obtain.command: GET {admin}/admin/serverinfo -> systemInfo.version  (or check /realms/{realm} response headers / release notes)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version is at/above the fixed release for all applicable Keycloak advisories

option_description: Whether this internet-facing IdP has had vendor security patches applied within the organization's defined patch SLA (e.g. critical CVEs within the committed remediation window).
security_impact: Triggers "IdP software exploitation (unpatched CVE)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when edge_appliance_patched_within_sla is false. Overdue patching governs how promptly published advisories (CVE-2024-8883 and companions) are remediated on an internet-facing IdP (T1190 / T1212).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the patch-management record for the IdP and confirm security patches were applied within the organization's committed remediation SLA.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Patch ledger shows recent advisories applied within the committed SLA window; no overdue security patches

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the running version against the advisory fixed-version list as evidence of current patch state.
how_to_obtain.command: GET {admin}/admin/serverinfo -> systemInfo.version  (or check /realms/{realm} response headers / release notes)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version is at/above the fixed release for all applicable Keycloak advisories

option_description: Whether the deployed IdP release is subject to at least one published, exploitable CVE (redirect-validation bypass, auth bypass, info disclosure, or RCE) for which no patch has been applied.
security_impact: Triggers "IdP software exploitation (unpatched CVE)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when unpatched_known_rce_cve is true. An unremediated known-exploitable advisory matching the running version is directly exploitable (T1190 / T1212).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running version and cross-reference it against the vendor security-advisory list (CVE-2024-8883 / CVE-2024-1132 / CVE-2023-6927 / CVE-2026-3872) to determine if an unremediated exploitable CVE applies.
how_to_obtain.command: GET {admin}/admin/serverinfo -> systemInfo.version  (or check /realms/{realm} response headers / release notes)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version is at/above the fixed release for all applicable Keycloak advisories

option_description: Whether the IdP runs as a multi-instance HA cluster (>=2 replicas) behind a load balancer with health probes, rather than a single instance.
security_impact: Triggers "IdP availability / DoS (single point of failure)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when clustered_ha_deployed is false. The IdP gates all federated authentication, so a single node is a single point of failure whose loss denies authentication to every RP (T1498 / T1499.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the IdP deployment topology and confirm multiple replicas behind a load balancer with health probes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Deployment topology shows >=2 IdP replicas, LB health probes, and rate limiting on the public auth/token endpoints

option_description: Whether volumetric/network DoS protection (upstream WAF/CDN/scrubbing or provider DDoS mitigation) fronts the public auth/token endpoints.
security_impact: Triggers "IdP availability / DoS (single point of failure)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when ddos_protection_in_place is false. Without it a network DoS against the internet-facing IdP denies authentication federation-wide (T1498 / T1499.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the network fronting the IdP and confirm upstream volumetric DoS protection (WAF/CDN/scrubbing or provider DDoS mitigation) protects the public auth/token endpoints.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Deployment topology shows >=2 IdP replicas, LB health probes, and rate limiting on the public auth/token endpoints
